data.description:
# ADR-0083's capability-detection guidance is unsafe on Python 3.12+ as written

## The gap

ADR-0083 ("Reconciler vendor adapter seam") §193-198 prescribes: "Callers detect a capability
by an `isinstance`-guarded check against the backend (a backend that does not implement
`SupportsLinks` is never asked to sync links) — capability is observed via behavior, not
structural introspection."

Since Python 3.12 (CPython gh-102433) a `@runtime_checkable` Protocol `isinstance` resolves
members with `inspect.getattr_static`, which deliberately does NOT see attributes served by
`__getattr__`. So the prescribed check returns a FALSE "capability absent" for any object
that proxies dynamically.

Measured while implementing `a3fa-e8d4-f4aa-4b51` (this checkout, Python 3.12):

    hasattr(proxy, "add_comment")                 -> True
    isinstance(proxy, SupportsComments)           -> False
    isinstance(MagicMock(), SupportsComments)     -> False   # has BOTH members

## Why it matters

Taken literally the guidance is actively harmful in exactly the situation the capability
Protocols exist for. A decorator/wrapper transport that forwards to an inner client — a
retry wrapper, an instrumentation shim, a recording proxy — HAS the capability but fails
`isinstance`, so a caller following the ADR would skip its writes and report the skip as
DESIGNED. That is the silent-soft-failure shape a3fa was filed to remove, reinstated with an
alert saying it was intended.

It also makes every `MagicMock`/`SimpleNamespace` transport double fail the check: an
isinstance-only guard broke 28 existing tests in the a3fa change before the fallback was
added.

a3fa resolved this LOCALLY by making its guard isinstance-primary with a
`hasattr(client, member)` fallback (`dispatch_apply_phases._capability_present`), pinned by
`test_proxying_transport_is_capable_and_is_not_skipped`. The ADR text was NOT changed — this
ticket is that follow-up, so the next caller reading §193-198 does not reimplement the hazard.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — ADR-0083 §193-198 is amended (in the ADR's own amendment style, as the
      `SupportsIncremental` removal note already does) to state that `isinstance` against a
      `@runtime_checkable` Protocol is necessary but NOT sufficient on Python 3.12+, citing
      the `getattr_static` behaviour and the proxying-transport consequence.
- [ ] AC2 — the amendment names the sanctioned shape (isinstance primary, member-level
      `hasattr` fallback) and points at `_capability_present` as the reference implementation.
- [ ] AC3 — any OTHER `isinstance(..., Supports*)` capability dispatch in the tree is
      enumerated and either confirmed proxy-safe or fixed; the enumeration is recorded here
      (search both semantically and for the Protocol names as strings).
- [ ] AC4 — no behaviour change is required of `_capability_present`; if the review concludes
      the fallback should instead be centralised for reuse, that is stated as a follow-up
      rather than done inline.

## Verify

- `grep -rn "isinstance(.*Supports" src/rebar`
- `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_capability_guard_a3fa.py -q`
data.title: ADR-0083's isinstance-only capability detection is unsafe on Python 3.12+
